text: John names this the revelation of Jesus Christ, given by God to show his servants what must soon take place.
Christ sent it by his angel to his servant John.
John testifies to the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
A blessing on the one who reads aloud and those who hear and keep what is written, for the time is near.
John writes to the seven churches in Asia: grace and peace from the one who is and was and is to come, the seven spirits, and Jesus Christ.
Jesus is the faithful witness, firstborn of the dead and ruler of kings, who loves us and freed us from our sins by his blood.
He made us a kingdom and priests to his God and Father; to him be glory and dominion forever.
He is coming with the clouds and every eye will see him; all tribes of the earth will mourn. Amen.
The Lord God says he is the Alpha and the Omega, who is and was and is to come, the Almighty.
John, a fellow sufferer in the kingdom, was on the island of Patmos because of God's word and the testimony of Jesus.
On the Lord's day he was in the Spirit and heard a loud voice like a trumpet behind him.
The voice told him to write what he sees in a book and send it to the seven churches, from Ephesus to Laodicea.
He turned and saw seven golden lampstands.
Among them stood one like a son of man, in a long robe with a golden sash.
His head and hair were white as wool, his eyes like a flame of fire.
His feet were like burnished bronze and his voice like many waters.
In his right hand were seven stars, a sharp two-edged sword came from his mouth, and his face shone like the sun.
John fell at his feet as though dead; he laid his right hand on John and said not to be afraid.
He is the first and the last, the living one who was dead and is alive forever, holding the keys of Death and Hades.
John is to write what he has seen, what is now, and what comes after; the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.
